+## What
+
+`xcrun xctest .build/out/Products/Debug/MLXLMTests.xctest` fails on the `stable` branch (HEAD 73cb5db plus the uncommitted work of ^jar6qq9, which changes no file in the MLXLMTests target graph). Two runs gave the same result: `Executed 694 tests, with 36 failures`, and `Test run with 1207 tests in 91 suites failed ... with 101 issues`.
+
+The failures are numeric tolerance failures:
+- XCTest: `GlmOcrContinuationTests`, `NanbeigeTests.testWarmContinuationMatchesFullPrefill`, `Qwen25VLContinuationTests`, `Qwen35ContinuationTests`, `Qwen3VLContinuationTests` (for example `0.0020094514 is greater than 0.001`), `testQwen35GDNCheckpointMatchesPrefixWithoutReplayingProjections`, `testQwen35VLMGDNCheckpointMatchesPrefix`, `testSSMAttnChunkedMatchesUnchunkedValuesAndGradients`.
+- Swift Testing: `attentionSinkChangesTheOutput`, `compressedLayerReadsTheCompressRopeTheta`, `decodeStepMatchesThePythonReference`, `prefillMatchesThePythonReference`, `theSortedRoutingPathAgreesWithTheUnsortedPath`, and the `theCollapse*` / `theExpand*` / `theHeadReduce*` / `theRoundTrip*` tests.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] Find the cause (OS or Metal change, or a code change) of the divergence.
+- [ ] `xcrun xctest .build/out/Products/Debug/MLXLMTests.xctest` passes with zero failures.
\ No newline at end of file

 assignees:

+comments:
+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01m3as1p4kq4r8yeh7hewfeptm
+  text: |-
+    ### Research — root cause found
+
+    Cause: TF32 on the GPU neural accelerators (NAX) of the Apple M5 Max. This is not a race and not a code change in this repository.
+
+    Evidence:
+    - The machine is an Apple M5 Max (Mac17,6), macOS 27.0 (26A428), Xcode 27.0 (27A266a), Metal toolchain 32023.921.
+    - mlx-swift 0.31.6 (pin 0bb916c, the same pin as at bc13b2f; `.build/checkouts/mlx-swift` is at this pin; Package.resolved did not change since 13ed148 on 2026-08-26).
+    - `mlx/backend/metal/device.h` `is_nax_available()` is true when macOS >= 26.2 and the GPU generation is >= 17 (M5). `mlx/utils.h` `enable_tf32()` reads `MLX_ENABLE_TF32` with the default 1. Thus `matmul.cpp` (lines 366, 962, 2402), `quantized.cpp` (694, 790, 1135) and `scaled_dot_product_attention.cpp` (177) send float32 inputs to NAX kernels that compute in TF32 (10-bit mantissa, unit roundoff 2^-11 = 4.9e-4).
+    - The NAX path is used only for some shapes. A warm continuation (8 new tokens) and a cold prefill (48 tokens) thus use different kernels with different precision. The difference 2e-3 to 2.8e-3 is 4 to 6 TF32 units of roundoff. A float32 path gives approximately 1e-6.
+    - A/B test on the same build: `xcrun xctest -XCTest MLXLMTests.NanbeigeTests` fails with 0.0028252602 > 0.001. With `MLX_ENABLE_TF32=0` it passes. The full bundle with `MLX_ENABLE_TF32=0`: 695 XCTest, 0 failures; 1207 Swift Testing tests in 91 suites passed.
+    - Upstream knows this: `Tests/MLXLMTests/SpeculativeDecodingTests.swift` line 33 says "on hardware with a NAX, float32 (the default dtype) runs in tf32 in batch mode and float32 in non-batch".
+    - The four other bundles pass without the change (MLXGuidedGenerationTests 70, MLXFoundationModelsTests 299, CXGrammarTests 7, MLXHuggingFaceMacrosTests 5).
+
+    About bc13b2f: the OS (macOS 27 boot on 2026-09-13 09:58, no boot since), the machine (setup 2026-03-13), Xcode (2026-09-03), the Metal toolchain mount (2026-09-14 07:00) and the mlx-swift pin are all older than bc13b2f (2026-09-14 13:44). I cannot find an environment change after bc13b2f. The NAX TF32 path was active on this machine at bc13b2f also. Thus the pass counts in the bc13b2f message probably come from a run that was not on this configuration. I cannot prove where they came from.
+
+    Plan: the tests compare float32 results with float32 tolerances. The tolerances are correct for float32 and are not correct for TF32. Do not change the tolerances. Make the MLXLMTests process compute float32 in float32: set `MLX_ENABLE_TF32=0` (if it is not set) when the test bundle loads, before the first MLX operation. MLX reads the variable one time in a static, so the set must occur at load time. Swift has no load-time hook, thus use a small C target with a constructor function.
